content.text:
The drawing shows a pyranose ring with an N-picolinoyl amide at C2 and acetates at C1, C3, C4 and C6. This looks like a 2-deoxy-2-picolinamido-glucopyranose tetraacetate, probably the β-anomer of the glucosamine derivative. No wedges or hashes are drawn, so I would not add stereo.

**Ring layout.** The ring oxygen is at the top right. Going clockwise from it:
- C1 (anomeric carbon) carries OAc, at the right.
- C2 carries NH, at the bottom right.
- C3 carries AcO, at the bottom left.
- C4 carries AcO, at the top left.
- C5 carries the CH2OAc group, at the top.

**Substituents.** The NH is acylated by C(=O) attached to pyridin-2-yl, and the ring N sits adjacent to the carbon bearing the carbonyl.

**Stereochemistry.** The bonds appear to be drawn as plain lines, and the instructions say to add stereo only where wedges or hashes are shown. I am therefore leaving all stereocentres unspecified.

**SMILES.** Starting from C1 and going around the ring:
C1(OC(C)=O) – C2(NC(=O)c3ccccn3) – C3(OC(C)=O) – C4(OC(C)=O) – C5(COC(C)=O) – O1.

Written out: CC(=O)OC1OC(COC(C)=O)C(OC(C)=O)C(OC(C)=O)C1NC(=O)c1ccccn1
